messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: page fired for service=billing-metering-ingest severity=high — reason=Token-count spike + downstream aggregation backlog (alert: metering.alerts.high_token_delta). auto-escalation in 5m if not acked

pagerduty: PagerDuty note: page routed to oncall: ashley (oncall). Incident ID: PD-89321

ashley (oncall): on it. joining. can someone paste the alert graph and recent commit?

miguel (billing-engineer): alert graph https://grafana.redwood.local/d/ingest/token-delta?panelId=4 spikes at 23:08 UTC, ingestion lag up ~12m, duplicate-write ratio up to 6%. last deploy to metering-ingest was 2026-03-12 21:42 UTC (rollout/kv-cache-change).

ken (sre): pinged. I've seen consumer-window mismatches before with the new consumer group checkpointing change. suspecting checkpoint->offset mapping drift causing consumers to reprocess chunks -> duplicates -> aggregator sees token storm.

ashley (oncall): are customers impacted? any invoice holds triggered yet?

miguel (billing-engineer): early checks: invoice pipeline flagged 18 accounts for potential overcount (threshold exceeded), but invoice sync hasn't run. risk: a subset of hourly invoices may be inflated if not corrected before billing run in 2h.

sara (billing-ops): flagged account IDs on slack DM to miguel. we need estimate ASAP to decide notify vs silent backfill.

ken (sre): mitigation plan: 1) pause upstream producers or throttle consumers to stop further duplicates; 2) switch aggregator reads to idempotent dedupe branch (standby) to drain; 3) run targeted backfill/repair for affected time windows; 4) consider temporary invoice hold for high-risk customers.

ashley (oncall): execute step 1 now. miguel/ken coordinate. I'll own comms and PD updates.

ken (sre): running commands now.
```bash
# pause kafka consumer group to stop processing new messages
kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --group metering-ingest --topic tokens.prod --reset-offsets --to-current --execute
# quick throttle as fallback
kubectl -n metering set resources deployment/metering-ingest --limits=cpu=50m
```

ken (sre): paused consumer group checkpoint commits and applied short throttle. confirm no new high deltas after 23:18 UTC.

miguel (billing-engineer): confirming: downstream aggregator ingest events dropped to baseline ~23:20. dupe ratio trending down. starting dry-run of idempotent aggregator branch (read-only) to validate dedupe logic.

ashley (oncall): ping @sara — please prepare a customer-impact summary template if we need to notify a small set. add: estimated affected invoices, earliest time window, mitigation timeline, SLA impact.

sara (billing-ops): on it. drafting now.

miguel (billing-engineer): dry-run shows dedupe removes ~96% of duplicate tokens for the reprocessed window. will run repair job to reconcile counters for affected windows. starting repair in 10m.

ken (sre): running repair with safety guards. using query with safelist to limit to accounts flagged. command:
```bash
python tools/reconcile_tokens.py --start 2026-03-13T22:50:00Z --end 2026-03-13T23:20:00Z --accounts-file flagged_ids.txt --dry-run
```

ken (sre): dry-run looks good. will run non-dry in 5m if no objections.

eve (support): if we need to notify customers proactively, what's the expected message? small group, possible billing discrepancy, will escalate to account teams once you confirm.

ashley (oncall): hold on external comms until repair completes. internal comms only for now — we don't want to cause panic. we'll prepare a cautious template in case we need to send.

miguel (billing-engineer): running non-dry repair now. estimated runtime 18m. I'll post progress every 5m.

incident-bot: pagerduty ack received from ashley (oncall) at 23:22 UTC — PD-89321 acknowledged. escalation paused.

ashley (oncall): thanks. ken, miguel update me at completion. sara prepare customer template but don't send. eve stand by for CS handoff.

ken (sre): repair completed at 23:42 UTC; reconciliation shows corrected token deltas for flagged accounts, deviations reduced under threshold. post-repair aggregator metrics normalized by 23:46.

miguel (billing-engineer): confirming: invoice-risk list cleared; no invoice sync ran during affected window. we'll re-run invoice preflight checks tomorrow and mark this incident in billing ops notes.

sara (billing-ops): good. holding off on external emails. prepping internal incident note for finance and acct teams.

ashley (oncall): moving to monitoring mode. leaving a short checklist for post-incident: 1) revert temporary throttle and consumer pause after 4h of stable metrics; 2) open a PR to rollback the problematic checkpoint mapping change or add a canary; 3) postmortem doc with timeline and customer-impact analysis. assign owners: ken for rollback PR, miguel for postmortem writeup + metric dashboards, sara for customer-impact and finance sync.

ken (sre): noted. I'll open emergency rollback PR and add a canary gate.

miguel (billing-engineer): I'll own the postmortem. starting notes now.

sara (billing-ops): I'll sync with finance and draft the customer comms in case we need later.

incident-bot: incident closed (manual). final status: mitigated, reconciliation done, no customer invoices impacted — monitoring for 4h. Incident ticket: PD-89321 -> closed.

ashley (oncall): thanks team. reactions :thumbsup: :tada: — will update status page if anything changes.
